taskVersion.name: deadline-math-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Standard set, reasoning allowed. Convert a published contest deadline to the reader's local time: day rollover, the weeks when the EU and US change clocks on different dates, 12 AM and AoE wording, non-hour offsets. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On September 30, 2026, Eastern Time (ET) will be observing Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is UTC-4. Madrid, Spain, will be observing Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2. The difference is +6 hours (Madrid is 6 hours ahead of ET).

Adding 6 hours to 5:00 PM ET (17:00 ET) gives 23:00 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru observes Peru Standard Time (PET), which is UTC-5. To convert 12:00 UTC to PET, subtract 5 hours.

12:00 UTC - 5 hours = 07:00 PET.

ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CEST (Central European Summer Time) is UTC+2. JST (Japan Standard Time, which is Tokyo's time) is UTC+9. Therefore, Tokyo time is 7 hours ahead of CEST (9 - 2 = 7).

Adding 7 hours to 9:00 AM CEST gives 4:00 PM (16:00) on the same day in Tokyo.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is in the Central European Summer Time (CEST) zone on October 11, 2026, which is UTC+2. Pacific Daylight Time (PDT) is UTC-7. Therefore, Madrid is 9 hours ahead of PDT. Adding 9 hours to October 11, 2026, 11:59 PM PDT, brings us to 8:59 AM on the following day in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is 9 hours ahead of Pacific Standard Time (PST) on March 3, 2026, as neither location will be observing Daylight Saving Time yet. Adding 9 hours to 11:59 PM PST on March 3 rolls the time over to the next day.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 08:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET is UTC+1. Los Angeles (PST in February) is UTC-8. Therefore, CET is 9 hours ahead of Los Angeles time. Subtract 9 hours from 10:00 AM CET.

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

JST (Japan Standard Time) is UTC+9. Lima, Peru (PET - Peru Standard Time) is UTC-5. This means Lima is 14 hours behind JST.

To convert 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026, to Lima time, we subtract 14 hours:
8:00 AM on May 5 - 14 hours = 6:00 PM on May 4.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PT (Pacific Time) on October 28, 2026, will be PDT (UTC-7) as Daylight Saving Time ends in early November. Madrid, Spain, on October 28, 2026, will be on CET (UTC+1) as Daylight Saving Time will have ended on October 25. Therefore, Madrid is 8 hours ahead of PT.

October 28, 2026, 11:59 PM PT + 8 hours = October 29, 2026, 7:59 AM in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is UTC+1 (Central European Time) in late October, as Daylight Saving Time typically ends on the last Sunday of October. Eastern Time (ET) on October 30, 2026, will be Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is UTC-4. Therefore, Madrid is 5 hours ahead of EDT.

9:00 AM EDT + 5 hours = 2:00 PM local time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 14:00

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET (Central European Time) is UTC+1. New York in late October observes EDT (Eastern Daylight Time), which is UTC-4. Therefore, CET is 5 hours ahead of EDT. Subtracting 5 hours from 18:00 CET gives 13:00 EDT.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PT (Pacific Time) on November 2nd will be PST (Pacific Standard Time), which is UTC-8, as Daylight Saving Time in the US ends on November 1st, 2026. Madrid, Spain, on November 2nd will be CET (Central European Time), which is UTC+1, as Daylight Saving Time in Europe ends on October 25th, 2026. Therefore, Madrid is 9 hours ahead of PT.

Adding 9 hours to November 2, 2026, 11:59 PM PT:
11:59 PM PT + 9 hours = 08:59 AM on November 3, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PT (Pacific Time) usually refers to PST (UTC-8) or PDT (UTC-7). On March 20, 2026, Daylight Saving Time will be active in the US, so PT will be PDT (UTC-7). Madrid will be on CET (UTC+1) because European Daylight Saving Time starts later in March. Therefore, Madrid is 8 hours ahead of PDT (UTC+1 - (UTC-7) = 8 hours).

Adding 8 hours to March 20, 2026, 11:59 PM PDT:
11:59 PM PDT + 8 hours = 7:59 AM the next day.

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 07:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On March 25, 2026, CET (Central European Time) is UTC+1. Los Angeles will be observing PDT (Pacific Daylight Time), which is UTC-7. The difference is 8 hours, with CET being ahead of PDT. Subtracting 8 hours from 12:00 PM CET results in 4:00 AM PDT on the same date.

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 12, 2026, Eastern Time will be EDT (UTC-4) and Madrid will be on CEST (UTC+2). Madrid is 6 hours ahead of EDT.
00:00 ET on October 12 + 6 hours = 06:00 on October 12.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 06:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) refers to the latest time any place on Earth will reach a specific time, which is effectively UTC-12. Madrid, Spain, on October 9, 2026, will be observing Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2 (as Daylight Saving Time in Europe typically ends later in October).

To convert 23:59 AoE (UTC-12) to Madrid time (UTC+2):
1. Convert AoE to UTC: 23:59 on October 9, 2026 (UTC-12) + 12 hours = 11:59 on October 10, 2026 (UTC).
2. Convert UTC to Madrid time: 11:59 on October 10, 2026 (UTC) + 2 hours = 13:59 on October 10, 2026 (CEST).

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 13:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PT (Pacific Time) in August is Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), which is UTC-7. Madrid, Spain in August is Central European Summer Time (CEST), which is UTC+2. Therefore, Madrid is 9 hours ahead of PT (2 - (-7) = 9). Adding 9 hours to 12:00 PM PT results in 21:00 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

IST (Indian Standard Time) is UTC+5:30. On November 10, 2026, Madrid will be observing CET (Central European Time), which is UTC+1. Therefore, IST is 4 hours and 30 minutes ahead of Madrid time. Subtracting this difference from the deadline: 11:59 PM IST - 4 hours 30 minutes = 7:29 PM CET.

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Nepal Time (NPT) is UTC+5:45. Lima Time (PET) is UTC-5.
Lima is 10 hours and 45 minutes behind Nepal (5:45 + 5 = 10:45).

Subtract 10 hours and 45 minutes from 2026-04-02 17:00 NPT.
17:00 - 10:45 = 06:15. The date remains the same.

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Adelaide (South Australia) will be observing Daylight Saving Time (ACDT) on October 6, 2026, making its time UTC+10:30. Madrid will be observing Central European Summer Time (CEST) on that date, making its time UTC+2.
The time difference is 10:30 - 2 = 8 hours and 30 minutes. Adelaide is ahead of Madrid.
To find the Madrid time, subtract 8 hours and 30 minutes from the Adelaide deadline:
10:00 AM on October 6, 2026 (Adelaide) - 8 hours 30 minutes = 01:30 AM on October 6, 2026 (Madrid).

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 01:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney is 8 hours ahead of Madrid at that time of year (Sydney will still be on Australian Eastern Standard Time, UTC+10, and Madrid will be on Central European Summer Time, UTC+2). Therefore, you need to subtract 8 hours from the Sydney time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 10:00
